messages.author: 695eaec5c92d8703
messages.subject: allow relative paths in Rsubread
parts:
Hi,

Others have noted that an error occurs when GTF is not in the current directory - for example, here: https://support.bioconductor.org/p/64524/ .  

I have noted similarly in using Rsubread that when the `files` argument is passed relative paths to bam files, the same error occurs.  

It would be good if Rsubread could accept relative paths in all cases without error.

One advantage of this would be that the paths that are printed during trace output would potentially be shorter, and thus fit on screen.  As it is they often get clipped.

Thanks,

~Malcolm Cook

messages.author: bce99ba71cd48eea
messages.subject: Re: allow relative paths in Rsubread
parts:
Hi Malcolm,

The relative paths are OK for RfeatureCounts. The post that you referred to used "~" in the path, which is not a file-system level abbreviation for "$HOME", but a shell-level abbreviation. Linux shell (eg, bash) or R can replace "~" to the path to your home directory, but RfeatureCounts doesn't do so. 

For example, you can use "../../hg19.GTF" as the annotation file, but you cannot use "~/hg19.GTF" -- you should use the home directory in the file names.

Cheers,
Yang

messages.author: 695eaec5c92d8703
messages.subject: Re: allow relative paths in Rsubread
parts:
Yang,

Right you are again!  My apologies for the report, indeed the mistake was mine.

Cheers again,

Malcolm
